name: Seated Cable Row
description: The seated cable row is a horizontal pulling exercise using a low-pulley cable machine. It trains the mid and upper back through scapular retraction and arm pulling, while maintaining a constant cable tension throughout the movement. It is particularly effective for developing back thickness and improving posture.

execution.starting_position: Sit on the seated row machine with feet on the foot rests, knees slightly bent. Grasp the cable attachment with both hands. Sit tall with a neutral spine and slight forward lean from the hips.
execution.setup_instructions: Attach a close-grip or straight bar handle. Set a weight that allows full range of motion with controlled form.
steps: Sit upright with a neutral spine, then row the handle toward the lower abdomen.
Drive the elbows behind the torso and squeeze the shoulder blades together firmly at the peak.
Slowly return the handle to the starting position, allowing the shoulder blades to protract fully for a complete stretch.
execution.breathing_instructions: Exhale as you row. Inhale as you return.
common_mistakes: Using excessive forward lean and momentum from the lower back to initiate each rep
Pulling the handle to the chest rather than the abdomen
Not allowing shoulder blades to fully protract at full extension
safety_considerations: Avoid rounding the lower back when leaning forward
Keep the torso upright throughout — only the arms and shoulder blades should move
execution.range_of_motion_guidance: Full protraction at the front, full retraction and row to the lower abdomen at the back.
coaching_cues: Sit tall as if a string is pulling your head to the ceiling
Row with your elbows, not your hands
